Dr. Joseph Galati says he’s seen a troubling shift in American healthcare over the past 10–15 years: doctors are examining patients less and less.

“Physicians aren’t examining their patients anymore. It’s becoming a thing of the past. When I see someone, they change into a gown and I examine them from head to toe. Patients ask, ‘What are you going to do to me?’ I ask, ‘Haven’t your other doctors examined you?’ They say, ‘No, they just sit and talk to me.’”

Insurance incentives are a major part of the problem:

- Appointments are often limited to just 10–15 minutes.
- Tests and medications are reimbursed at higher rates than the time-consuming work of a thorough examination.

We need to get big money out of healthcare.
